tests.description: Attached is not working. WebMCP is pull-only, so a bound agent has the whole catalog and no instruction — and rendering nothing here left the page at its most capable showing nothing to act on, which is the state a person reads as "it connected and then did nothing".
tests.key: AgentHandoff › asks the person to start an agent that is attached but idle

tests.description: The full attach pitch is still wrong here: the agent is already attached, so two doors and an MCP command are answers to a question this person no longer has.
tests.key: AgentHandoff › does not re-pitch attaching to an agent that is already attached

tests.description: The demoted band is a SUBTRACTION, and presence-only assertions cannot see a subtraction come undone. The steps and the seed quote are written for a first meeting; putting them back here is the drift this pins.
tests.key: AgentHandoff › drops the first-meeting steps and quote from the reattach strip

tests.description: The finished-plan screen. `MapScreen` is an `h-screen` flex column and this strip is `shrink-0`, so every row it takes comes out of the summary the person came back to read — the dense variant drops the heading line and puts both commands on one row. Both commands must SURVIVE the shrink: dropping one would be a smaller strip that no longer does its job.
tests.key: AgentHandoff › drops the heading but keeps both commands when dense

tests.description: The deliberate subtraction. `HandoffReattach` is for someone who has attached before and knows which door they use, so it shows the command flat with no three-way choice around it. A tab strip appearing here would be the full band's onboarding leaking back into the screen that exists to not have it.
tests.key: AgentHandoff › gives the reattach strip the command flat, with no tabs

tests.description: The default is the full strip — a component that silently rendered its compact form everywhere would pass the dense test above and still be wrong on every working map.
tests.key: AgentHandoff › keeps the heading on the reattach strip by default

tests.description: The MCP command is the half of the reattach strip an AGENT can act on — the start prompt is for the person. Losing it would leave the strip naming a door without opening it, which is the state the whole change is a fix for.
tests.key: AgentHandoff › offers the MCP command alongside the prompt when reattaching

tests.description: The full band opens on the route that works for EVERY agent — the bare endpoint — not on one client's command. This is the fact the panel used to get wrong: it offered `claude mcp add` and nothing else, so a reader holding ChatGPT desktop or Cursor was shown a command they cannot run and never shown the address they needed.
tests.key: AgentHandoff › opens the full band on the endpoint every agent can use

tests.description: The ORDER is the change, so asserting only presence would let the old arrangement back in unnoticed — the panel used to open with the explanation and reach the prompt third, which is exactly the layout that still passes a presence-only check.
tests.key: AgentHandoff › puts the instruction before the explanation in document order

tests.description: The command did not go away, it moved behind the tab that owns it. Driven rather than asserted on a hidden node: a tab that renders its panel but never responds to a click is the failure this catches, and it looks identical to a working one in any static query.
tests.key: AgentHandoff › reaches the Claude Code command through its tab

tests.description: The case that would drift. `working` means a tool is mid-flight, and that agent still sees this map when its turn comes round — so it counts as attached, exactly as askPresence treats it. If this and the node-question composer ever disagreed, one page would contradict itself.
tests.key: AgentHandoff › renders nothing once the attached agent has actually worked the map

tests.description: The instruction has to be ON the panel at all — it is the sentence the panel existed without, and the one someone arriving actually needs.
tests.key: AgentHandoff › renders the instruction and both steps

tests.description: Steps are numbered because their order is the content. An unordered list renders the same words and loses the only thing making them instructions.
tests.key: AgentHandoff › renders the steps as an ordered list

tests.description: The reported case: someone submitted an idea, nothing is attached, and the log holds only their own root node.
tests.key: AgentHandoff › renders when nothing is attached and no agent has worked the map

tests.description: No provider at all — an isolated scenario. useOptionalWebMcpBridge returns null rather than throwing, and absence is honest absence.
tests.key: AgentHandoff › renders without a bridge provider at all

tests.description: The prompt is the useful part, and it is useless without the id.
tests.key: AgentHandoff › shows a start prompt naming this map

tests.description: A brief-started map has no sentence, so the panel must not render empty quote marks where the person's words would go.
tests.key: AgentHandoff › shows no quoted idea for a map started from a brief

tests.description: Reopening a map an agent has already contributed to, in a browser with no agent. The full pitch would be wrong — but so is showing nothing: this is exactly the state where someone needs the way back in, and rendering null left them with a header saying "No agent attached" and no route to change that.
tests.key: AgentHandoff › still offers a way back in on a map an agent has already worked

tests.description: The reported failure, pinned: on a map that already holds real work, the sequence must say why it declined and must NOT write. Asserting the log line alone would pass even if the writes went out anyway, so the assertion that matters is the one about `callTool`.
tests.key: AgentSimulator › declines the demo sequence on a map with real work, writing nothing

tests.description: The panel opens collapsed. Rendering it at all is now an opt-in the map page makes deliberately, so once it IS rendered the launcher must be there — otherwise the opt-in leads nowhere.
tests.key: AgentSimulator › renders the launcher collapsed

tests.description: The guard has to REFUSE the wrong map without refusing every map — a demo that never runs is as broken as one that always does, and it is the failure mode a fail-safe default invites.
tests.key: AgentSimulator › runs the sequence on a map holding only its seed

tests.description: A map deleted underneath an open tab is the one reason that stays on the line. Every other reason is context someone can go looking for; this is an error they have to act on, and a page that knows the tab is dead must not decline to say so.
tests.key: AgentStatus › keeps a deleted map visible without a click

tests.description: The removal was unconditional, not a fix scoped to the unavailable state — a header that showed the counter only once an agent attached would pass the test above and still put debugging output in front of a person.
tests.key: AgentStatus › keeps the badge off an attached agent too

tests.description: The detail did not leave the product, it moved behind a click — so the click has to work, both ways. A panel that opens over the map and cannot be put away again would be worse than the permanent badge it replaced.
tests.key: AgentStatus › opens the detail on click and closes it again

tests.description: The state the badge was worst in: "No agent attached" reads as a failure, and an unexplained `r14` beside it reads as the build that failed. The bridge is handed a revision here specifically so the header has one to leak.
tests.key: AgentStatus › states presence without a revision badge beside it

tests.description: The same argument as the revision badge, applied to the tool count. "Agent attached · 9 tools" answered a question nobody in front of a map asks, and spent header room doing it. The number is not deleted — it is one click away — so the guard has to be that it is absent UNTIL then.
tests.key: AgentStatus › states presence without a tool count beside it

tests.description: Closing must not be a one-way door: nobody closes a thing they cannot get back, so the pill has to restore the conversation intact.
tests.key: BoardChat › brings the conversation back from closed

tests.description: An answer wears the colour of the card it answered. The panel is what wires the log to the map: without the nodes and themes reaching it, every answer would render neutral and the rule would silently not exist.
tests.key: BoardChat › colours an answer with the theme of the card it answered

tests.description: An empty send would post a blank turn into the transcript, which reads as the person having said nothing on purpose.
tests.key: BoardChat › does not send an empty message

tests.description: Collapsing hides the transcript and KEEPS the input row — that is what makes it different from closing. "The chat is always here" is a claim the input row makes, so collapsing must not withdraw it.
tests.key: BoardChat › hides the transcript but keeps the input when collapsed

tests.description: The state every new board starts in. An empty conversation must read as inviting rather than broken — it is the first thing anyone sees, so it is the one state that must not look like a failure to load.
tests.key: BoardChat › is present and usable with nothing said yet

tests.description: The mixed case, which is the real one: a log is never all conversation or all board movement, and the filter has to hold while both are present.
tests.key: BoardChat › keeps the conversation when board events are mixed into the log

tests.description: Closing has to genuinely uncover the board — that is the whole reason the state exists — so the input row goes too.
tests.key: BoardChat › leaves only a way back in when closed

tests.description: The channel says what it is. The code has always documented this input as the slot for everything the partner did not think to ask about; until the label arrived, nothing on screen said so.
tests.key: BoardChat › names itself as the general channel

tests.description: A log of ONLY board-visible events is, as far as the conversation goes, an empty one — and must render like one rather than as an empty scroller.
tests.key: BoardChat › reads as empty when the log holds only board-visible events

tests.description: An answer belongs in the conversation as the words the person said, not as a reference to the card it closed — the card already shows that.
tests.key: BoardChat › renders an answer as the words that were said

tests.description: An answer to a card since deleted must render as an ordinary bubble, not as an error and not in a colour that lies about which theme it belongs to.
tests.key: BoardChat › renders an answer whose card is gone without breaking

tests.description: The recorded shape is `{ id, text }` per question — see the `question.asked` write in `toolRuntime`. Stringifying the object gave EVERY agent-asked question the bubble "[object Object]", which is the whole of what the partner said arriving as noise.
tests.key: BoardChat › renders an asked question as its words, not as its object

tests.description: The two sides of the exchange, each on its own side of the panel. Without this a transcript is a wall of text with no way to tell who said what.
tests.key: BoardChat › renders what each side said

tests.description: A turn that lands behind a collapsed panel is indistinguishable from one that did not land at all.
tests.key: BoardChat › reopens itself when you say something while collapsed

tests.description: The panel is where you say something that applies to the whole map rather than to whichever card is nearest — so sending has to work.
tests.key: BoardChat › reports what was typed into it

tests.description: The editorial rule, stated directly. These three kinds are the board MOVING; repeating them here would turn the conversation into a debug log.
tests.key: BoardChat › says nothing about the events you can already see on the board

tests.description: The case the old reducer could not express: one event closing two cards was joined into a single bubble with " · ", which would need one background to be two colours.
tests.key: BoardChat › splits one answer event across two cards into two coloured bubbles

tests.description: A log written by an older or hand-rolled caller should degrade to its words rather than to noise — it costs one branch and the alternative is the same failure again from a different direction.
tests.key: BoardChat › still reads a question recorded as a bare string

tests.description: Two answers to differently-themed cards must not look alike, or the transcript is back to one undifferentiated column.
tests.key: BoardChatBubble › gives two themes two different colours

tests.description: Colour now carries meaning that alignment used to carry alone, and the panel is narrow — so the partner's turn still has to read as theirs.
tests.key: BoardChatBubble › keeps the partner's turn visually distinct from yours

tests.description: A general note is about the whole map, so it has no theme to wear. It must not borrow one — a default colour would claim a theme the remark does not belong to.
tests.key: BoardChatBubble › leaves a general note uncoloured

tests.description: An answer wears its card's colour. This is the rule in one assertion.
tests.key: BoardChatBubble › paints an answer in the hue of the theme it belongs to

tests.description: Sides, kept: the partner on the left, you on the right.
tests.key: BoardChatBubble › puts the two sides on opposite sides of the panel

tests.description: The deleted-card case: an answer to a node that is gone renders as an ordinary bubble rather than as an error or as a colour that lies.
tests.key: BoardChatBubble › renders an answer with no resolvable theme exactly like a note

tests.description: A map with nothing at the far end yet hands down an EMPTY stream rather than omitting the prop — the stack's own empty state is what draws the honest marker, and it can only do that if it is mounted.
tests.key: BoardWorkspace insight stream › hands the board an empty stream on a map with no insights

tests.description: The claim the feature rests on: a themeless insight reaches the board, with no round finished and nothing answered anywhere on the map.
tests.key: BoardWorkspace insight stream › hands the board an insight before any round is finished

tests.description: The rule the stack rests on, asserted through the workspace rather than only through `insightStream`: a node of an insight kind that lives inside a theme is a card in that row, not a claim about the whole idea. Get this wrong and the same node is drawn twice on one plane.
tests.key: BoardWorkspace insight stream › leaves a themed insight in its row rather than on the stack

tests.description: The first revision it sees only SEEDS the reference. Refreshing on mount would re-fetch the page the person just loaded — a wasted round trip on every single board open, and a visible flash for nothing.
tests.key: BoardWorkspace live refresh › does not refresh on the first revision it sees

tests.description: A retried or out-of-order poll can report a revision BEHIND the one already seen. Treating that as a change would refresh backwards and then forwards again on the next poll — the loop, arrived at from the other direction.
tests.key: BoardWorkspace live refresh › does not refresh when the revision goes backwards

tests.description: A poll that returns the same revision is the NORMAL case — it is what the bridge reports most of the time. Refreshing on it would put the page in a permanent refresh loop driven by its own polling.
tests.key: BoardWorkspace live refresh › does not refresh when the revision repeats

tests.description: No agent is bound inside an iframe, which is the state EVERY preview and capture genuinely produces — so an unbound bridge is the common case, not an edge one. Read as zero it would look like a revision, and every board that later bound an agent would refresh spuriously.
tests.key: BoardWorkspace live refresh › ignores an unbound bridge rather than reading it as zero

tests.description: The sequence a real session produces: bind, then several advances. Each one is a refresh, and none of them is a double.
tests.key: BoardWorkspace live refresh › refreshes once per advance across a run of them

tests.description: The contract itself: the map moved, so the server component has to re-run. Exactly once — this is the only thing that makes the board live.
tests.key: BoardWorkspace live refresh › refreshes once when the revision advances

tests.description: Binding late is the ordinary path: the page renders, then the bridge reports a revision for the first time. That first real number is a seed, not an advance — refreshing on it is the mount bug wearing a hat.
tests.key: BoardWorkspace live refresh › treats the first real revision after an unbound start as a seed

tests.description: Without this, dragging on the buttons pans the map underneath them — the control moves the thing it is supposed to be fixed against.
tests.key: BoardZoomControls › does not let a drag on the controls pan the board

tests.description: The glyphs are +, − and All, so the accessible names are the only thing a screen reader or a test can address them by.
tests.key: BoardZoomControls › names every control for anyone not looking at it

tests.description: Each control has to reach its own handler. Two buttons wired to one callback is a bug you only notice when zooming out zooms in.
tests.key: BoardZoomControls › reports each control separately

tests.description: Bottom-LEFT. The conversation sits in the bottom-right, and the two sharing one corner is exactly what this arrangement exists to undo.
tests.key: BoardZoomControls › sits in the corner opposite the conversation

tests.description: The box lives inside the form whose submit starts a map. Enter has to mean "attach this link" here, or the keystroke starts a board on a half-typed idea instead.
tests.key: BriefLinkBox › attaches on Enter instead of submitting the form

tests.description: Enter on an empty box means nothing, the same as the dead button does.
tests.key: BriefLinkBox › does nothing on Enter with an empty box

tests.description: A way out that does not attach anything is the difference between opening this by accident and being stuck in it.
tests.key: BriefLinkBox › reports a cancel without attaching

tests.description: The whole job: report the address upward, trimmed, and retrieve nothing.
tests.key: BriefLinkBox › reports the address and fetches nothing itself

tests.description: Whitespace is not an address. Someone who hits space then Attach should get the same nothing as someone who typed nothing.
tests.key: BriefLinkBox › treats whitespace as empty

tests.description: An empty box has nothing to attach, and a live button that does nothing is worse than a dead one that explains itself by being dead.
tests.key: BriefLinkBox › will not attach an empty address

tests.description: While a file is being read, offering to read another is a way to lose the first one.
tests.key: BriefMenu › cannot be opened while a file is being read

tests.description: Escape is the gesture someone reaches for when a popover appeared over the thing they were reading. The old panel needed no dismissal; this does.
tests.key: BriefMenu › closes on Escape

tests.description: Clicking away is the other dismissal, and the one people try first.
tests.key: BriefMenu › closes when the click lands outside it

tests.description: With a document in hand the button stops inviting one and starts reporting the one attached — the state the dashed panel used to make obvious.
tests.key: BriefMenu › names the attached brief instead of inviting another

tests.description: Every capability the dashed panel advertised has to survive the collapse, and the link door added to it, which means all three must appear on the one click that opens the menu.
tests.key: BriefMenu › offers all three ways in once opened

tests.description: The file picker is the panel's "Choose a file" button, one level deeper.
tests.key: BriefMenu › reports the file choice and closes behind it

tests.description: The link route is the one that reaches a page nobody can upload — a Notion doc, a client's own site — and it closes behind itself like the others.
tests.key: BriefMenu › reports the link choice and closes behind it

tests.description: The paste route is the panel's "Paste it instead" link, and the door for anyone working from a document they cannot upload.
tests.key: BriefMenu › reports the paste choice and closes behind it

tests.description: The trigger stopped being a bare `+` and started saying what it takes. That label IS the fix for drag-and-drop reading as missing: a symbol with no noun invites nobody to drop anything on it.
tests.key: BriefMenu › says what it accepts rather than showing a bare plus

tests.description: At rest it is a single button and nothing else. If the menu rendered its items eagerly the collapse would have bought no space at all.
tests.key: BriefMenu › shows no menu items until it is opened

tests.description: The popover is a real menu to a screen reader, and the button says whether it is open — the panel's two plain buttons needed neither, this does.
tests.key: BriefMenu › states its expanded state on the trigger

tests.description: The confirmation is a swapped glyph, which a screen reader cannot see. The live region is the only channel that carries it.
tests.key: CopyTextButton › announces the copy in a live region once it succeeds

tests.description: The case this component is most careful about. A browser can refuse clipboard access, and with selection suppressed on the board there is no fallback path — so a control that said "Copied" after copying nothing would send someone away to paste something that is not there.
tests.key: CopyTextButton › does not claim success when the clipboard refuses

tests.description: Hidden at rest and revealed on hover would make the control invisible in every captured scenario, so a card that is the board's focused one shows it outright. Both states have to be reachable or the reveal is not a reveal.
tests.key: CopyTextButton › is hidden at rest and shown when its card is the focused one

tests.description: The button sits ON a card that takes a click to focus itself, and ON a board that reads a drag as a pan. Both have to be held off: `data-no-pan` is what the camera's pointerdown guard looks for, and stopping propagation is what keeps the card underneath from grabbing the board's attention.
tests.key: CopyTextButton › keeps the press to itself — no pan, no focus of the card underneath

tests.description: Nothing on screen shows what this button would copy — that is the whole difference from `CopyablePrompt` — so the string it was given reaching the clipboard unaltered is the only guarantee there is.
tests.key: CopyTextButton › writes exactly the text it was given

tests.description: Promoted to the primary action, the confirmation cannot be a purely visual signal — a live region is what makes the flip reach a screen reader too.
tests.key: CopyablePrompt › announces the copied state in a live region

tests.description: The counterpart, and the reason the fix is a per-tone decision rather than a blanket one: `inline` exists to hold ONE row inside the reattach strip, so wrapping it would defeat the only thing it is for.
tests.key: CopyablePrompt › does not wrap the inline tone, which is a deliberate one-row control

tests.description: The other half of the same rule, and the half that would go quiet if the ink treatment were reverted: the promoted tone is a filled ink pill with light text on it, because it sits on the paper surfaces where an outline would not read as the one thing to do.
tests.key: CopyablePrompt › fills the primary tone with ink and light text

tests.description: The label flip is the entire success signal there is.
tests.key: CopyablePrompt › flips the label once the copy succeeds

tests.description: The tone prop exists so promoting the handoff caller cannot restyle the others, which only holds if the default is genuinely unchanged. This used to assert the default carried no `bg-lime`, which distinguished the two tones only while `primary` was the lime one. Now that no call to action in the product is lime, that assertion passes for BOTH tones and so pins nothing — it would survive the default being handed the primary's fill, which is the one regression it exists to catch. What separates th
tests.key: CopyablePrompt › leaves the default tone unfilled

tests.description: The deliberate failure behaviour. A browser can refuse clipboard access, and when it does the button must neither throw nor claim it worked — the prompt stays on screen and the label stays as an offer.
tests.key: CopyablePrompt › neither throws nor claims success when the clipboard is refused

tests.description: The text stays on screen whatever the clipboard does, because select-and-copy by hand is the path underneath every other failure.
tests.key: CopyablePrompt › renders the prompt text

tests.description: The reported bug. A long origin-bearing MCP command is a single unbreakable token wider than the box that holds it, and the `default` tone was the one tone with no wrapping rule at all — so it rendered OUTSIDE its rounded border instead of inside it. A CLASS assertion rather than a measured overflow, deliberately: jsdom has no layout, so nothing in this suite can observe a box being overflowed. The class is the thing that is either there or not, and it is what the fix changed; the visual claim i
tests.key: CopyablePrompt › wraps a long command inside the default tone box

tests.description: A button that copies something OTHER than what is displayed would be the worst version of this bug: silent, and only discovered after pasting.
tests.key: CopyablePrompt › writes exactly the displayed text to the clipboard

tests.description: The emitter, the check script and the eval command all have to name the same file. This constant is what stops them disagreeing.
tests.key: DEFAULT_EVAL_SCHEMA_PATH › points at the committed fixture path

tests.description: Every step is a REAL call against the bound catalog, so a step with no explanation would leave a viewer unable to tell what it demonstrated.
tests.key: DEMO_SEQUENCE › explains every step it runs

tests.description: read_brief comes BEFORE read_map: an agent handed a long document orients on its outline before deciding what to pull, and the scripted turn is the only place that ordering is written down.
tests.key: DEMO_SEQUENCE › orients on the brief before reading the map

tests.description: The turn has to end somewhere a person can act, and the slice is where WebMCP cannot bind — a preview has no live agent, so this scripted step is the only way the slice path is exercisable at all.
tests.key: DEMO_SEQUENCE › proposes a slice that names what it would settle

tests.description: The sequence is the closest thing here to a written description of one agent turn: say what you are about to do, read, add, ask, report back. Losing the ask would make it a demo of writes rather than an exchange.
tests.key: DEMO_SEQUENCE › walks a full turn including the question that waits on the person

tests.description: A prose hint renders without the monospace pill styling, so a sentence never reads as a command you are meant to type.
tests.key: ErrorScreen › keeps a prose hint out of the command pill

tests.description: The title renders as the heading element, so the diagnosis is what a screen reader and the page outline lead with.
tests.key: ErrorScreen › leads with the title as the heading

tests.description: The action slot renders only when given one, so states with no next move offer no affordance leading nowhere.
tests.key: ErrorScreen › renders an action only when one is passed

tests.description: Neither renders when omitted, which is the production case and the one a screenshot cannot distinguish from a failed render.
tests.key: ErrorScreen › renders neither when they are omitted

tests.description: Both the command pill and the Prisma detail line appear when supplied.
tests.key: ErrorScreen › renders the command and detail when given them

tests.description: A name that already fits is shown as it is — truncation is for names that need it, not a house style.
tests.key: FirstCardAttachments › leaves a short name alone

tests.description: Almost every arrival is carrying nothing, and an empty list would still take vertical space in a card whose emptiness is the point.
tests.key: FirstCardAttachments › renders nothing when the card is carrying nothing

tests.description: Files are named rather than indexed, because the list is re-ordered by nothing and identified by name everywhere else in this card.
tests.key: FirstCardAttachments › reports removing a browsed file by name

tests.description: Removing one names WHICH one. The card carries several links now, so a bare "a link was dropped" would leave the caller guessing — and the guess it would make is the first, which is the one you least often mean.
tests.key: FirstCardAttachments › reports removing a link by its source

tests.description: Both kinds at once is a real state — someone can browse for a doc and point at a page — and the two have to coexist rather than replace.
tests.key: FirstCardAttachments › shows a brief and browsed files together

tests.description: The state the change exists for: an idea usually arrives with a repo AND a doc AND somebody else's page, and the card used to allow the first and then grey the control out. They all wear the same chip — which one becomes the board's brief is a fact about the map's shape, not a ranking the person needs to be shown.
tests.key: FirstCardAttachments › shows every link that was added, not only the first

tests.description: A long source name truncates rather than growing. The full name stays in the label so it is still recoverable by anyone who needs it.
tests.key: FirstCardAttachments › truncates a long source name but keeps it whole in the label

tests.description: Shows that the question cards are still drawn on screen at the camera's lowest zoom, instead of the board emptying out to hubs and lines.
tests.key: GalaxyBoard card visibility › keeps the cards on the board at the minimum zoom

tests.description: Shows that a board with enough themes to frame below the old cutoff still displays every card the moment it opens, with no gesture from anyone.
tests.key: GalaxyBoard card visibility › opens a many-theme board with its cards drawn, not just its hubs

tests.description: Shows the hub's theme label on screen alongside the cards when zoomed far out, which is the one job the scale threshold still has.
tests.key: GalaxyBoard card visibility › still draws the hub label beside the cards when far out

tests.description: Development offers the one command that fixes it. The pill is the whole reason the route's extra fields are carried back rather than dropped.
tests.key: IdeaPrompt › offers the fix a failing route named

tests.description: A failure no route ever saw, so nothing upstream could have made it JSON.
tests.key: IdeaPrompt › reads a proxy failure carrying HTML as a sentence

tests.description: The happy path still has to work — an error-handling change that broke creation would pass every assertion above.
tests.key: IdeaPrompt › routes to the new map when creation succeeds

tests.description: THE PRODUCTION HALF, and the one no development capture can show: the same failure, with the classifier having withheld the command, must render the sentence and no pill at all.
tests.key: IdeaPrompt › shows no fix when the route withheld one

tests.description: A route that classified the failure gets to say what it found; the component must show that rather than its own fallback.
tests.key: IdeaPrompt › shows the sentence a failing route stated itself

tests.description: THE REPRODUCTION. A 500 with an empty body is what the drifted database produced, and it is the shape that has no JSON to read.
tests.key: IdeaPrompt › surfaces a server failure without leaking a parse error

tests.description: The other half of the same contract: an attached agent means the band must NOT be there, and a screen that never mounts it also passes that. Asserting both is what makes the pair meaningful.
tests.key: MapScreen › leaves the band off when an agent is attached

tests.description: The regression this pins: the band was a dangling import for the whole of the board redesign. It type-checked, and every AgentHandoff test kept passing, because they all render the band directly. Nothing asserted the screen put it on the page — so a person on a map with no agent got the header's "No agent attached" and no route to change that.
tests.key: MapScreen › mounts the handoff band when no agent is attached

tests.description: The brief travelled from the route to the band through this screen, and the merge dropped the middle leg: `brief` was declared as a prop and never read. `handoffCopy` is already pinned on both sides of `hasBrief`, so what is untested without this is the WIRING — and the cost of getting it wrong is handing someone a start prompt naming the wrong entry point.
tests.key: MapScreen › names read_brief in the start prompt when the map has a brief

tests.description: The control for the case above. Without it, a screen that hardcoded `hasBrief` true would pass the brief assertion while getting every brief-less map — most of them — wrong.
tests.key: MapScreen › names read_map when there is no brief

tests.description: The kind has to be in the accepted set at all — this is what makes it wake an agent parked on await_user_activity rather than sitting inert.
tests.key: POST /api/maps/:id/exchange — user.question › accepts user.question as a user-writable kind

tests.description: Asking about a node must not change it. The person has not decided anything yet, so marking, reopening or reordering the node would be the route inventing an act they did not perform.
tests.key: POST /api/maps/:id/exchange — user.question › leaves the node it asks about untouched

tests.description: The ordinary case, and the reason the label is denormalised: the rail names the node, and it should not have to re-query per row to do it.
tests.key: POST /api/maps/:id/exchange — user.question › records the question with the node label resolved

tests.description: The check that matters. A node on somebody else's map must be refused, not logged here — otherwise the ownership boundary the route already keeps for the map itself has a hole in it at the payload.
tests.key: POST /api/maps/:id/exchange — user.question › refuses a node that belongs to a different map

tests.description: A question about a node that does not exist at all is the same refusal — there is nothing for it to be about.
tests.key: POST /api/maps/:id/exchange — user.question › refuses a nodeId that names nothing

tests.description: Without an id this is a note wearing a question's name, and the agent is back to guessing which pill was meant.
tests.key: POST /api/maps/:id/exchange — user.question › refuses a question with no nodeId

tests.description: The effect is keyed on the phase, not on every render. A re-render from an unrelated parent update must not yank the track back, which would fight a reader who has just scrolled it by hand.
tests.key: PhaseNav active-step visibility › does not re-scroll when the phase is unchanged

tests.description: Exactly one pill carries `aria-current="step"` — the hook the scroll effect targets and the only cue a screen reader gets, since the lime fill that marks the active step visually says nothing on its own.
tests.key: PhaseNav active-step visibility › marks only the active phase as the current step

tests.description: The design decision this locks in: at narrow widths the track SCROLLS rather than collapsing to a "3 of 6" summary, because it is a map of the process rather than a progress bar. All six stay in the DOM at every width.
tests.key: PhaseNav active-step visibility › renders every phase, so the whole process stays reachable

tests.description: A page can load with any phase active — a map resumed at Explore starts with the track already scrolled past the start. If the pill were only centered on CHANGE, that first paint would open scrolled to 01 with the real position off-screen.
tests.key: PhaseNav active-step visibility › scrolls the active pill into view on first render

tests.description: The behavior the narrow track exists for: advancing a phase has to bring the new step into view on its own. Without it the active step can sit off the right edge with nothing telling the reader it moved.
tests.key: PhaseNav active-step visibility › scrolls the newly active pill into view when the phase advances

tests.description: The reported case, and the reason this plan exists. A track that fits has nothing hidden past either edge, so a fade there is a promise of content that does not exist — and it is drawn straight over the active lime pill.
tests.key: PhaseNav edge fades › applies no fade at all when the whole track fits

tests.description: A window can cross the fits / does-not-fit boundary without any scrolling at all. Left to the scroll listener alone, a track that just became wide enough to fit would keep a fade it no longer has any content to justify.
tests.key: PhaseNav edge fades › drops the fade when a resize makes the track fit

tests.description: The mirror of the reported bug. Scrolled hard against the end, the trailing fade has to go — otherwise the active pill is washed out again, this time on a track where the fade looked justified.
tests.key: PhaseNav edge fades › drops the trailing fade once the track is scrolled to the end

tests.description: Content is cut off both ways, so both edges earn a fade. This is the state the mask exists for, and the only one where the old behaviour was right.
tests.key: PhaseNav edge fades › fades both edges mid-track

tests.description: Parked at the start of a track that genuinely does overflow: there is more to the right and nothing to the left, so exactly one edge should say so.
tests.key: PhaseNav edge fades › fades only the trailing edge at the start of an overflowing track

tests.description: The decision has to track the reader, not just the first paint. Without the scroll listener the fade would be frozen at whatever was true on mount, which is the static-decoration bug wearing a different disguise.
tests.key: PhaseNav edge fades › re-derives the fade when the reader scrolls the track

tests.description: Sub-pixel widths mean scrollLeft rarely lands exactly on its maximum, so a strict equality check would leave the trailing fade stuck on at an end the reader has visibly reached. Half a pixel short still counts as the end.
tests.key: PhaseNav edge fades › treats a sub-pixel gap at the end as the end

tests.description: What most real answers look like: one of the guesses, and the part the guess missed. Neither half was sayable with the other before.
tests.key: QuestionCard — a shortlist › joins the options taken to the words typed

tests.description: Not answering is a real answer to give. A board that only lets you proceed by answering turns "I don't know yet" into a made-up answer, which the partner cannot tell from a real one — and the question stays OPEN, so the bar keeps counting it and it comes round again.
tests.key: QuestionCard — a shortlist › offers a way past a question without answering it

tests.description: A first answer on a card with no options has nothing to go back to, so offering Cancel there would be a control that does nothing.
tests.key: QuestionCard — a shortlist › offers no Cancel when there is nothing to cancel back to

tests.description: An isolated fixture has nowhere to move on TO, and a Skip that goes nowhere is worse than no Skip at all.
tests.key: QuestionCard — a shortlist › offers no Skip where there is nowhere to skip to

tests.description: Every list the partner writes is a guess about what you might say, and the guess must never be the only thing you are allowed to say. The box is now present ALONGSIDE the options rather than replacing them, so the two can be combined instead of chosen between.
tests.key: QuestionCard — a shortlist › offers the box for what the list does not contain, beside the list

tests.description: The change this card exists for. "Two of those" is an ordinary answer and the card could not record it at all.
tests.key: QuestionCard — a shortlist › records several options as one answer

tests.description: The structural regression that cost the most. The card's root was a `button` first, which is invalid HTML — a button may not contain other buttons, so the parser HOISTS the inner ones out of it and they stop being clickable. The options silently became decoration.
tests.key: QuestionCard — a shortlist › renders its options as real buttons, not decoration

tests.description: The card turns over the instant it is answered, before the map has caught up. Answering writes to the shared log and the board re-renders from the server when the revision rises — a round trip — so without this the card someone just answered still looks unanswered, which reads as the board having eaten the answer.
tests.key: QuestionCard — a shortlist › shows the answer on the card immediately, before the map catches up

tests.description: Picking one no longer ANSWERS. It used to, which made a shortlist a cage: one option or nothing, and no way to qualify the one you took. Save is what records, and until it is pressed nothing has been said.
tests.key: QuestionCard — a shortlist › takes an option without answering on the spot

tests.description: Save must not be gated on the FIELD when the answer is not only in the field. Options taken with nothing typed is a complete answer.
tests.key: QuestionCard — a shortlist › will not record a blank, but will record options alone

tests.description: An answer is a thought at a moment, and thinking is what this board is for. The pencil is the whole of what makes an answer revisable.
tests.key: QuestionCard — an answered question › returns to an editable box through the pencil

tests.description: Your words are the content and the question becomes their label — that inversion is what makes an answered card read as a statement rather than as a form with the fields missing.
tests.key: QuestionCard — an answered question › shows the answer with the question demoted to a label

tests.description: The bug this card had: `approach` is not an insight KIND, so a card carrying a diagram fell through to the answered-question branch and the diagram — the entire content of the card — was never drawn, while the layout had already given it the wide column.
tests.key: QuestionCard — an insight › draws a diagram it carries even when its kind is not an insight kind

tests.description: The same hole, on the image side: a reference card exists so someone can LOOK at the thing.
tests.key: QuestionCard — an insight › draws a picture it carries even when its kind is not an insight kind

tests.description: The eyebrow reads the word for the KIND rather than a generic label, which is what lets the board be read without a legend.
tests.key: QuestionCard — an insight › names the kind it is

tests.description: An explicit product requirement, and nothing else defended it: an unanswered card must LOOK typeable before anyone has clicked anything. The one thing a first-time user has to discover is that these are typed into, so the affordance has to exist before the interaction that would reveal it.
tests.key: QuestionCard — an open question › carries a field without having to be clicked first

tests.description: The eyebrow comes from `cardEyebrow`, the same helper every other card in the app uses. A second implementation of one design rule drifts, and the rule it guarantees — an answered question stops calling itself Open — is one this card would otherwise be re-deriving.
tests.key: QuestionCard — an open question › names its state with the shared eyebrow vocabulary

tests.description: Typing and sending, through the control a person actually uses.
tests.key: QuestionCard — an open question › reports what was typed when it is saved

tests.description: An empty answer is not an answer. Saving one would close the question against a blank, which reads on the board as answered-with-nothing.
tests.key: QuestionCard — an open question › will not save an empty answer

tests.description: Regression two, and the subtler one: `role="button"` fixed the markup but not the meaning. An element's accessible name is computed from its contents, so the card announced itself as a button named after its own entire text — swallowing its controls into one label and producing ambiguous matches for assistive technology and for tests alike.
tests.key: QuestionCard — structure › does not announce itself as a button either

tests.description: Regression one. A `button` may not contain the option pills and the pencil; the parser hoists them out, leaving them unclickable. The card is a CONTAINER — the controls inside it are what should be buttons.
tests.key: QuestionCard — structure › is not itself a button

tests.description: Clicking the card brings it into focus — a convenience on top of the real controls, which is why it takes the click without taking a role.
tests.key: QuestionCard — structure › reports a click as a request for focus

tests.description: While questions are open the cards are the action, so the footer counts and offers nothing to press.
tests.key: RowFooter › counts while the round is still being answered

tests.description: The end of the loop has no further step, so there is nothing to offer even though the round is finished and settled.
tests.key: RowFooter › offers nothing at the end of the loop

tests.description: Once the wait has settled, the action takes over from the count.
tests.key: RowFooter › offers the phase action once the wait has settled

tests.description: THE ONE A SCREENSHOT CANNOT MAKE. The round is done and the map is still reaching, so the shimmering row above is already explaining the wait. Anything here would be the same thing said twice, one line apart — which is exactly what the first build of this did, and what looked wrong on screen.
tests.key: RowFooter › renders nothing while the map is still reaching for the next round

tests.description: A round of statements was never something to answer, so it must not show a "0 of 0 answered" line on its way to the action.
tests.key: RowFooter › shows no count for a round that asked nothing

tests.description: The cap itself: three rows, and the count in the control tells you what you are not seeing rather than hiding that there is more.
tests.key: SavedMapList › caps the strip at three and says how many there are

tests.description: Usually empty, and an empty strip is still a heading and a gap — so it renders nothing rather than reserving space for nothing.
tests.key: SavedMapList › renders nothing when no maps are saved

tests.description: The reachability half of the trade — nothing is lost, only folded.
tests.key: SavedMapList › reveals the rest on request

tests.description: Under the cap there is nothing to disclose, so the control must not appear.
tests.key: SavedMapList › shows every map and no disclosure when it fits

tests.description: Exported so the ask and any surface that wants to say "one short" read the same number. A second copy of it somewhere else is the drift to prevent.
tests.key: TARGET_LIVE_INSIGHTS › is a positive target the ask can be measured against

tests.description: Muting is what keeps the dust from competing with a card being read. It changes only the opacity of the whole field — the particles themselves must not move, or focusing a card would make the galaxy reshuffle behind it.
tests.key: ThemeParticles › dims without redrawing the field

tests.description: A different galaxy must look like a different galaxy. If the seed were ignored, every cluster on the board would wear the same dust in a different colour — which reads as one cluster drawn repeatedly.
tests.key: ThemeParticles › draws a different field for a different hue

tests.description: The property the whole component rests on: same hue in, same field out. Two renders are what a server pass and a client pass amount to.
tests.key: ThemeParticles › draws an identical field from the same hue

tests.description: It is decoration sitting behind the thing you are reading, so it must not reach the accessibility tree or take a click meant for a card.
tests.key: ThemeParticles › stays out of the way of the board

tests.description: Hue 0 is a real place on the colour wheel and a falsy value in JavaScript. A truthiness check anywhere in the chain would quietly send it somewhere else, so it has to produce a field like any other hue.
tests.key: ThemeParticles › treats hue zero as a hue rather than as absent

tests.description: The name is part of the contract between the route that writes the cookie and the pages that read it, so it is exported rather than typed twice.
tests.key: VISITOR_COOKIE › is a stable non-empty cookie name

tests.description: The regression this file exists for: WebMcpBridge renders copy promising these tools are reachable, so all seven must actually appear beside it.
tests.key: WebMcpBridge - NoAgent › renders every catalog tool rather than an empty list

tests.description: WebMcpBridge renders its resting state — the one every preview and capture shows. It must say an agent is absent, with a reason, rather than looking broken or, worse, claiming a connection it does not have.
tests.key: WebMcpBridge - NoAgent › reports that no agent is attached, with a reason

tests.description: A tab left open across a map's deletion. The binding is intact and the browser is still attached, so every ordinary signal reads "connected" — while each registered tool answers "No such map". The first agent to meet this reported the app as broken to the person using it, which is the cost of a page that cannot tell a dead map from a dropped request.
tests.key: WebMcpBridge - NoAgent › says the map is gone when the log 404s, rather than claiming a binding

tests.description: With nothing outstanding, WebMcpBridge shows the trigger rather than the answer block, and displays a zero count.
tests.key: WebMcpBridge - NoAgent › shows nothing awaiting an answer

tests.description: Answering releases the agent, and WebMcpBridge renders its resting state again. The answer must reach the log too, since an agent that already gave up can only find it there.
tests.key: WebMcpBridge - pending states › clears the questions and records the answer once the person replies

tests.description: WebMcpBridge renders the none-to-some boundary: exactly one question outstanding, with its text on screen.
tests.key: WebMcpBridge - pending states › renders a single outstanding question

tests.description: WebMcpBridge displays both questions and shows the status flipped to working — the agent's turn is paused until the person answers.
tests.key: WebMcpBridge - pending states › renders both questions and marks the agent as working

tests.description: The many state: WebMcpBridge renders all five full-sentence questions rather than truncating to the first few.
tests.key: WebMcpBridge - pending states › renders every question when an agent asks several at once

tests.description: The failure this pins is silent and total: Zod STRIPS keys a schema does not declare, so a `fromRefs` missing from `nodeShape` would be dropped before the planner ever saw it — every citation lost, no error anywhere.
tests.key: add_nodes carries the ask for insights › accepts the sources an insight cites and passes them through

tests.description: The vocabulary the schema binds to is NODE_KINDS, so the two new kinds reach the agent for free — but "for free" is exactly the kind of claim worth a test, since a hand-maintained enum here would silently reject them.
tests.key: add_nodes carries the ask for insights › accepts the two kinds an insight is usually written as

tests.description: An insight drawn from the whole map has no single source, so the field has to be genuinely optional rather than a required empty list.
tests.key: add_nodes carries the ask for insights › leaves the field off entirely when the agent cites nothing

tests.description: The ask itself. It is prose, and prose is easy to delete by accident — but it is the only thing telling the agent there is a target at all, so these pin the three claims it has to keep making.
tests.key: add_nodes carries the ask for insights › states the target, what a themeless node means, and how to cite

tests.description: The common case, and the one that proves this is a filter rather than a gate: a file that fits arrives with no message attached to it.
tests.key: admitFiles › admits files that fit

tests.description: Already at the cap. There is no room to partially fill, so the answer is nothing plus a sentence — never a silent no-op, which would look to the person like the paste simply failed.
tests.key: admitFiles › admits nothing once the map is already full

tests.description: Browsing twice for the same file is an ordinary slip, and listing it twice would leave two chips that both claim to be the same thing.
tests.key: admitFiles › ignores a file already in hand

tests.description: An oversize file is dropped but its companions still land — refusing the whole batch over one member would lose files the person can keep.
tests.key: admitFiles › keeps the rest of a batch when one file is too big

tests.description: At the cap, the ones that fit are kept and the person is told what happened rather than silently losing the overflow.
tests.key: admitFiles › takes only what there is room for, and says so

tests.description: Other query params are none of its business — a map opened with a filter or a tracking param on the URL must not accidentally summon the panel.
tests.key: agentPanelRequested › ignores unrelated query params

tests.description: The reported case, and the default: an ordinary dev session with no opt-in. This is the one that was previously true for every map in development.
tests.key: agentPanelRequested › is false for a plain map URL in development

tests.description: A bare `?agentPanel` with no value. Next hands this over as an empty string, which is not the opt-in.
tests.key: agentPanelRequested › is false for a valueless agentPanel param

tests.description: `=1` exactly, not any truthy string. Someone turning the panel OFF by editing the URL to 0 would be badly served by a truthiness check, which would read "0" as present-and-therefore-on.
tests.key: agentPanelRequested › is false for agentPanel=0

tests.description: The gesture itself. A person types it; nothing stumbles onto it.
tests.key: agentPanelRequested › is true when agentPanel=1 is present

tests.description: A repeated param arrives as an array. Reading the first entry keeps a doubled `?agentPanel=1&agentPanel=1` working the way it plainly means, rather than failing a strict string comparison against an array.
tests.key: agentPanelRequested › reads the first entry when the param is repeated

tests.description: The case that was wrong: no binding, but the log shows an agent mid-session.
tests.key: agentPresence › counts an agent working through the MCP door as attached

tests.description: The person's own writes are not an agent being present. Counting them would make every map claim an agent the moment someone typed into it.
tests.key: agentPresence › does not mistake the person for an agent

tests.description: The failure the window is sized to prefer. A turn spent reading a brief can leave a real gap between two writes, and dropping to "nobody is here" in the middle of one agent's turn is the exact bug the window exists to fix.
tests.key: agentPresence › holds presence through a gap inside one turn

tests.description: The empty case, which is most maps most of the time. It must report plain absence rather than a null-ish shape the callers have to interpret — three components read this to decide what to tell a person.
tests.key: agentPresence › is honest about a map no agent has ever touched

tests.description: The other half of honesty: an agent that left must stop counting, or the page promises someone a reply that is not coming.
tests.key: agentPresence › lets presence lapse once the window has passed

tests.description: The log arrives as JSON from the poll and as Dates from the server render.
tests.key: agentPresence › reads a timestamp that arrived as a JSON string

tests.description: A bound page can be ASKED — ask_user puts a question in front of a person and waits. A map reached over HTTP cannot, so the channel has to survive even when both signals are true.
tests.key: agentPresence › reports webmcp when the page is bound, whatever the log says

tests.description: Latest wins, not last-in-array: the poll appends, but nothing guarantees order across a merge of the initial render and a later page of events.
tests.key: agentPresence › takes the most recent agent event rather than the last one listed

tests.description: The rule this function exists to hold: a question is CREATED open and UPDATED when it is answered, so `createdAt` dates the ASKING. Reading it here would make every insight look current however far the thinking moved.
tests.key: answeredAt › dates an answer by when it was given, not when the question was asked

tests.description: A question still open is not an answer, and an insight is not a question.
tests.key: answeredAt › ignores unanswered questions and everything that is not a question

tests.description: Timestamps arrive as a Date from Prisma and as a string after a JSON round trip. An unparseable one sorts as epoch rather than NaN, which would make every comparison against it false and silently drop it from every count.
tests.key: answeredAt › reads a Date, an ISO string, and a value it cannot parse

tests.description: An answered call is a success, and its status is what an agent branches on.
tests.key: answeredResponse › marks the result answered and is not an error

tests.description: The agent needs both the question and the answer, since it may have asked several and cannot match them up from the answers alone.
tests.key: answeredResponse › reports each question with the answer it received

tests.description: The log holds every kind of event; only answers are answers.
tests.key: answersByNodeId › ignores events that are not answers

tests.description: Editing an answer is posting a second one, so the later answer must stand. If the first won, the Edit affordance would silently do nothing.
tests.key: answersByNodeId › lets a later answer replace an earlier one for the same question

tests.description: The ordinary case — one question, one answer, shown back on its card.
tests.key: answersByNodeId › reads a single answer back by its question id

tests.description: One user.answer can settle several questions at once.
tests.key: answersByNodeId › reads every answer out of a multi-answer event

tests.description: Day one: nothing has been answered, and every card is still asking.
tests.key: answersByNodeId › returns nothing for an empty log

tests.description: One malformed payload must not blank every other answer on the map.
tests.key: answersByNodeId › skips malformed entries without losing the good ones

tests.description: Latest is by revision, not by array position — the caller is not required to have sorted the log first.
tests.key: answersByNodeId › takes the highest-revision answer when the log arrives out of order

tests.description: The reported bug, as a test: two identical cards on the board where the agent made one call and a retry.
tests.key: applyToolCalls › does not duplicate nodes when a call is retried with the same requestId

tests.description: The other half of the contract, and the reason the fix keys on the request rather than the content: an agent may legitimately ask a similar question twice, and two genuine calls must both land.
tests.key: applyToolCalls › keys on the requestId rather than the content

tests.description: The second defect the fix closes. The writes used to run outside any transaction, so a throw partway through the insert loop left nodes on the map with no events and no revision bump — a state no agent reading the log can reconcile, and one that also renders as an unexplained card.
tests.key: applyToolCalls › leaves nothing behind when a write fails partway through the batch

tests.description: A retry of a call that created a theme and several nodes must leave exactly one of each — the dedupe covers everything the call wrote, not just the first table it touched.
tests.key: applyToolCalls › leaves one theme and one set of nodes when a multi-write call is retried

tests.description: Idempotency is opt-in. A call that supplies no key is not a retry and must write, or every caller that never adopted the convention silently stops working.
tests.key: applyToolCalls › writes on every call when no requestId is given

tests.description: Nothing is genuinely nothing.
tests.key: approxPages › counts an empty document as zero pages

tests.description: A short brief is still one page, never zero.
tests.key: approxPages › counts any non-empty document as at least one page

tests.description: A negative count is nonsense input; it must not produce a negative page.
tests.key: approxPages › never returns a negative page count

tests.description: Roughly 1,800 characters to the page, rounded.
tests.key: approxPages › scales with length

tests.description: The label has to change too. A send control reading "Ask the agent" with nothing attached is the exact overpromise this module exists to prevent.
tests.key: askPresence › drops the promise of a reply from the send label when nothing is attached

tests.description: With someone listening the control should say what it does — ask — rather than the neutral "send" that reads the same in both worlds.
tests.key: askPresence › names the agent in the send label when one is listening

tests.description: Guarding the negative directly: no branch may promise an answer from an agent that is not there.
tests.key: askPresence › never claims an agent will answer when none is attached

tests.description: Both branches must be usable copy — an empty string would render as a control with no label and a blank line where the honesty should be.
tests.key: askPresence › returns non-empty copy in both states

tests.description: The wake is the real mechanism and worth saying, because it is what makes asking different from leaving a note.
tests.key: askPresence › says asking wakes the agent when one is listening

tests.description: The whole point: absence is stated, not glossed over.
tests.key: askPresence › says plainly that no agent is attached when none is

tests.description: The two states must be distinguishable, or the UI is not actually telling the person which case they are in.
tests.key: askPresence › says something different in each state

tests.description: Several nodes asked about across a session all keep their marks.
tests.key: askedNodeIds › collects every distinct node across the log

tests.description: The ordinary case: the id travels in the payload, which is the whole reason this is its own kind rather than a note with a name in the prose.
tests.key: askedNodeIds › collects the node a question names

tests.description: A node asked about twice is still one marked node — the mark says whether, not how many.
tests.key: askedNodeIds › counts a node asked about twice only once

tests.description: Every other kind in the log must leave the marks alone — notes and answers carry node ids too, and marking those would badge half the map.
tests.key: askedNodeIds › ignores every other kind of event

tests.description: A map nobody has touched yet must produce no rows at all, so the rail can show its own explanation of how anything gets into it.
tests.key: askedNodeIds › is empty for an empty log

tests.description: A payload that lost its id must not throw and must not mark anything — one unattributable question should not take the marks off the rest.
tests.key: askedNodeIds › skips a question with a missing or non-string nodeId

tests.description: Deliberately shorter than `handoffCopy`'s prompt and carrying no id: the tools are already bound to THIS map, so an id would be a fact the agent has to ignore rather than one it needs.
tests.key: attachedStartCopy › carries no map id, unlike the unattached hand-off prompt

tests.description: The one sentence that stops an attached-but-idle map reading as a broken app. Without it the person sees "Agent attached" and nothing happening, and has no way to learn that a page cannot start an agent's turn.
tests.key: attachedStartCopy › explains why an attached agent is still not working

tests.description: Every slot the component renders must be filled in both branches — an empty eyebrow or instruction would render as a blank row above the prompt.
tests.key: attachedStartCopy › fills every slot for both entry points

tests.description: The same instruction said in plain words, because an agent that follows tool names but still narrates its answer has not put anything on the map. The prompt now also asks for a chat note, which is the opposite-looking change and must not be allowed to dissolve this one: the note is a POINTER ("here is what I put on the map"), and the thinking still has to go on the map. So this pins the division of labour rather than the old sentence.
tests.key: attachedStartCopy › keeps the deconstruction on the map, not in chat

tests.description: The prompt has to send the thinking to the MAP. "Deconstruct the idea" is something a model satisfies beautifully in its own chat window, and the first real agent given that prompt did exactly that — tidy paragraphs back in the chat, and a board still showing nothing.
tests.key: attachedStartCopy › names the write tools, not just the read

tests.description: A map that arrived with a document should be read from the document. The read tool is the one thing that differs between the two entry points.
tests.key: attachedStartCopy › reads the brief when there is one and the map when there is not

tests.description: An unknown id — including one belonging to a different board, which is deliberately indistinguishable — is answered with the way to find a real one, so the agent's next move is obvious rather than a retry.
tests.key: attachmentNotFound › names the tool that lists the real ids

tests.description: A text document is text. No image block, because there is no picture — returning an empty one would make every caller check for a block that is never populated.
tests.key: attachmentToolResult › hands a text document back as its text

tests.description: The headline. An image has to arrive as an image block carrying its media type and base64 that round-trips — a caption alone would be the exact failure this feature exists to fix.
tests.key: attachmentToolResult › hands an image back as a picture the agent can look at

tests.description: The picture still needs saying what it is. An image block with no caption is a thing with no provenance — the agent should know what it is looking at before it looks at it.
tests.key: attachmentToolResult › names the picture in text alongside it

tests.description: Every branch is an ordinary answer, never a fault. An `isError` result invites the blind retry that a permanent condition can never satisfy — which is exactly what a legacy row and a PDF both are.
tests.key: attachmentToolResult › never reports any of these as a fault

tests.description: An id is a cuid, not a secret. A list carrying one from another map must be ignored rather than reach that map's rows — the scoping is the access rule.

tests.description: Clearing has to leave NOTHING behind — an orphaned row would go on rendering in the "brought along" strip with no file behind it.
