tests.description: The count cap. It names the way out — remove one — rather than only the limit, because the limit alone is not an action.
tests.key: fitsAttachmentCaps › refuses one past the count cap

tests.description: The id is the whole point of the line: without it the agent can see that a picture exists and has no way to open it — a dead end.
tests.key: formatAttachmentLines › names the tool and the id that opens each attachment

tests.description: Most maps have nothing attached. A bare "Brought along" heading over an empty list would read as something that failed to load, so there is no section at all rather than an empty one.
tests.key: formatAttachmentLines › renders no section at all when nothing is attached

tests.description: Saying WHICH kind it is lets the agent decide whether the call is worth making before it spends the context on one.
tests.key: formatAttachmentLines › says what kind of thing each attachment is

tests.description: The load-bearing claim: this is metadata. If a size can be stated without the bytes, the bytes were never fetched — which is what keeps read_map cheap however large the attachments are.
tests.key: formatAttachmentLines › states a size without carrying any file content

tests.description: A legacy row has nothing to open, so it must NOT offer an id — sending the agent to read_attachment only to be told there is nothing there spends a call to learn what this line already knew.
tests.key: formatAttachmentLines › withholds the id from a row with no file behind it

tests.description: An empty section is a real state — a heading with nothing under it.
tests.key: formatCharCount › formats zero

tests.description: Thousands are grouped, because a bare 12690 reads as an id in a column of otherwise short numbers.
tests.key: formatCharCount › groups thousands

tests.description: Below a thousand there is nothing to group and no separator should appear.
tests.key: formatCharCount › leaves a short count alone

tests.description: How far behind the board is. The whole point of measuring it from the newest insight is that the agent is told a gap rather than left to feel one.
tests.key: formatInsightStanding › names how many answers have landed since the newest insight

tests.description: Day one, and the state every fresh map produces. A map that has done nothing wrong must not be told it is short — it should be told what an insight IS, which is the more useful thing on turn one.
tests.key: formatInsightStanding › reads as an invitation rather than a shortfall when there are none

tests.description: A number the agent can compare itself against is actionable in a way that "consider adding insights" is not. That is the design decision, and losing the figures would quietly turn the mechanism back into a mood.
tests.key: formatInsightStanding › states the budget as figures the agent can measure itself against

tests.description: The seed idea is preserved verbatim through the whole product; the MCP view must not be where it gets paraphrased away.
tests.key: formatMapDetail › includes the title, phase and verbatim seed idea

tests.description: A map created through MCP has no conversation yet; an empty section would read as a truncated response.
tests.key: formatMapDetail › marks an empty conversation explicitly

tests.description: A map whose nodes have all been removed still has to render.
tests.key: formatMapDetail › renders a map with no nodes

tests.description: A client needs both views to reason about the map the way the UI does.
tests.key: formatMapDetail › renders the conversation and the node tree under their own headings

tests.description: Without the id the client cannot open or modify the map it just listed.
tests.key: formatMapList › leads each row with the id in brackets

tests.description: One map per line keeps the response parseable by a client or a person.
tests.key: formatMapList › puts each map on its own line

tests.description: Phase and counts are how a client picks which map is worth opening.
tests.key: formatMapList › reports the phase and the node and message counts

tests.description: A client asking for maps on a fresh install needs a sentence, not a blank response it might read as a failure.
tests.key: formatMapList › says so plainly when there are no maps

tests.description: Without the cursor the agent cannot re-park exactly, and would either miss a map or re-read one it already handled.
tests.key: formatNewMaps › hands back the cursor to resume from

tests.description: '1 new maps' is exactly the kind of thing that survives review and then reads as broken.
tests.key: formatNewMaps › keeps the count singular for a single map

tests.description: The id is what every follow-up tool call takes; a row without it is a dead end, exactly as in formatMapList.
tests.key: formatNewMaps › leads each row with the map id

tests.description: One wait can hand back several maps, and the count must agree with itself.
tests.key: formatNewMaps › renders every map when several arrive at once

tests.description: The expiry case. An agent looping on this sees it constantly, so it must read as an ordinary answer and still carry the cursor.
tests.key: formatNewMaps › reports an empty result as normal rather than as a failure

tests.description: A blank line where the idea should be reads as missing data rather than as a map that genuinely started from a document.
tests.key: formatNewMaps › says so explicitly when a map has no seed idea

tests.description: A brief-started map's seed idea is empty or near-empty, so the brief is the thing worth reading first.
tests.key: formatNewMaps › spells out read_brief as the next call for a brief-started map

tests.description: The agent has to be told what to do next, not left to infer it.
tests.key: formatNewMaps › spells out read_map as the next call for a sentence-started map

tests.description: A handful of bytes is still something rather than nothing: "0KB" beside a file that plainly exists reads as a bug.
tests.key: formatSize › never rounds a real file down to zero

tests.description: The size an actual screenshot tends to be. Megabytes with a decimal would render most real attachments as "0.0MB", which says nothing.
tests.key: formatSize › reads kilobytes below a megabyte

tests.description: The unit the caps are stated in, so the refusal sentence and the chip beside it agree about what "5MB" looks like.
tests.key: formatSize › reads megabytes for a file measured in them

tests.description: Nothing at all is the legacy row, which should say nothing rather than claim a size it does not have.
tests.key: formatSize › says nothing for a row with no file behind it

tests.description: Non-question nodes may be open for their own workflow reasons; they must not make an agent wait for an answer nobody owes.
tests.key: formatStandingWait › ignores open nodes that are not questions

tests.description: Open questions are the contract: the reply must tell an agent exactly how to park itself until the person supplies the missing context.
tests.key: formatStandingWait › names the open-question count and the revision to wait from

tests.description: The wait it prescribes must fit inside the host's tool-call budget. This asserted 300 once, which is precisely the value that made every wait die in transit — so it is pinned against the shared default rather than retyped, and the old number is named as forbidden.
tests.key: formatStandingWait › prescribes a wait short enough for a host to actually return

tests.description: Once everything is answered there is nothing to wait for, and an added instruction would wrongly prevent the agent from moving the map forward.
tests.key: formatStandingWait › returns no guidance when every question is answered

tests.description: The agent is the only thing that reads this text, and the person is the only one who can answer. A reply that parks the agent without sending it to chat leaves someone staring at a map that never said anything was owed.
tests.key: formatStandingWait › sends the agent to chat to say what it did and what is needed

tests.description: Two calls landing on one port would mean the probe socket was never really released — the failure that would silently collide two servers started back to back.
tests.key: freePort › does not hand out the same port twice in a row

tests.description: The contract all three callers depend on. A number in the right range would satisfy a shape assertion while naming a port something else already holds, so the proof that the port is usable is using it.
tests.key: freePort › returns a port that can actually be bound

tests.description: The log speaks the contract's language, not the column's. A reader of the exchange log should learn what an insight came out of without having to know that SQLite made it a string.
tests.key: fromRefs resolution › carries the resolved ids on the node.added event as an array

tests.description: An insight drawn from the whole map genuinely has no single source, and a node that named nothing must be indistinguishable from one written before the field existed — not one carrying an empty array nobody can render.
tests.key: fromRefs resolution › leaves the column null when the agent named no sources

tests.description: The whole reason this is a ref and not an id: an insight almost always cites questions created moments earlier in the very same call, so a ref written through raw would be a citation pointing at nothing.
tests.key: fromRefs resolution › turns refs from the same call into the ids the database just minted

tests.description: An id that resolves to nothing is written through rather than dropped, the same call `resolveRef` already makes for parentRef: a citation naming nothing is a mistake worth being able to see in the row, and the read side drops it at render time so it never reaches the person.
tests.key: fromRefs resolution › writes an unresolvable ref through, and the read side drops it

tests.description: A bad id renders the not-found body, and the tab above it should say the app's name rather than sit blank or repeat the id.
tests.key: generateMetadata › falls back to the app name when the map does not exist

tests.description: Metadata runs a frame before the body. A throw here 500s the route before the page can render the error it was going to explain, so a failed read takes the same branch as no map at all.
tests.key: generateMetadata › falls back to the app name when the read throws, rather than 500ing

tests.description: Only `open` nodes count. Answered ones are already dealt with, so folding them in would make the badge read as work that is still waiting.
tests.key: generateMetadata › prefixes the open-question count when questions are waiting

tests.description: A zero in parentheses reads like a notification badge that never clears, so a fully-answered map shows its bare name instead of `(0)`.
tests.key: generateMetadata › shows the bare title when nothing is open

tests.description: The log may account for some of the map and not the rest — a seeded map that was then worked on. The explained part keeps its rounds and the remainder is appended by depth rather than dropped.
tests.key: groupIntoRounds › appends nodes the log never mentioned after the rounds it explained

tests.description: A phase set immediately after a round is what that round moved the thinking to, so the row can name itself after the phase instead of its number.
tests.key: groupIntoRounds › attributes a phase set immediately after a round to that round

tests.description: A phase set further downstream belongs to whatever round actually preceded it, so an unrelated round must not claim it.
tests.key: groupIntoRounds › does not attribute a distant phase set to an earlier round

tests.description: A seeded scenario, or a map written before any of this shipped, has no log to read. It must still draw as rows rather than as nothing.
tests.key: groupIntoRounds › falls back to grouping by depth when there is no event log

tests.description: The map is co-authored, so the person's own contribution is a round of its own rather than being folded into whichever agent batch it fell between.
tests.key: groupIntoRounds › gives a user-added node its own round between two agent batches

tests.description: The log arrives ordered in practice, but the grouping must not depend on the caller having sorted it — contiguity is about revisions, not position.
tests.key: groupIntoRounds › groups by revision even when the events arrive out of order

tests.description: One add_nodes call writes its events inside one transaction, so they share a contiguous revision run and one origin — that run is one row.
tests.key: groupIntoRounds › groups one contiguous run of adds into one round

tests.description: An id in the log with no node on the map is a node deleted since. It must not produce an empty row, and must not take the rest of its round with it.
tests.key: groupIntoRounds › ignores logged ids whose nodes are no longer on the map

tests.description: The root is the map's subject, not one of its answers. A row that mixed it in with the first batch would read as though somebody had asked it.
tests.key: groupIntoRounds › keeps the root alone even when its add is contiguous with the next batch

tests.description: THE case this module exists for. Both batches are children of the root, so both sit at depth 1; grouping by depth would merge them into one row and lose the fact that the agent asked twice.
tests.key: groupIntoRounds › keeps two batches at the same tree depth as two separate rounds

tests.description: Sibling order is the map's own, so a row reads left to right the way the agent meant it to rather than in whatever order the log happened to land.
tests.key: groupIntoRounds › orders the cards in a round by their sibling order

tests.description: The seed idea alone, which is every map on day one.
tests.key: groupIntoRounds › puts a lone root in a single round

tests.description: Nothing to group is not an error state — an empty map renders its invitation.
tests.key: groupIntoRounds › returns no rounds for a map with no nodes

tests.description: A finished map still holds every working node; only the four summary kinds belong on this screen.
tests.key: groupSummaryNodes › ignores kinds that do not belong on the summary screen

tests.description: Slices and next steps answer different questions — "interview three teachers" is not something you build — so neither bucket may swallow the other.
tests.key: groupSummaryNodes › keeps slices and next steps in separate buckets

tests.description: The screen must render its empty hints rather than crash on a map that reached the phase with nothing filled in.
tests.key: groupSummaryNodes › returns empty buckets for an empty map

tests.description: Next steps are numbered on screen, so their sequence is meaningful — rendering them in insertion order would mislabel the plan.
tests.key: groupSummaryNodes › sorts each bucket by order, not by input position

tests.description: Each region of the summary screen must draw from its own kind, or findings land in the wrong card.
tests.key: groupSummaryNodes › splits nodes into the summary buckets

tests.description: The whole point: three lines of a long idea used to scroll inside a three-row box, so most of what someone had written was hidden while they were still writing it.
tests.key: grownHeight › grows to fit what has been written

tests.description: A short idea does not get a tall box. The field holding its floor is what keeps the card's empty space — the space that says "this is yours to fill".
tests.key: grownHeight › holds the floor for something short

tests.description: The boundary itself, which is where an off-by-one would show as a field that scrolls one line early or one line late.
tests.key: grownHeight › is exact at the ceiling

tests.description: But not without end. The field lives on a card, and a card that grew with an essay would run off the screen the essay was being typed onto — so past the ceiling it goes back to scrolling, which is the honest trade.
tests.key: grownHeight › stops at the ceiling rather than running off the card

tests.description: The wait these prompts ask for has to be one a host will actually let return. Both carry the number as a literal — this module stays free of the catalog so a client bundle does not pull zod in for one integer — so the pinning has to happen here, where importing it is free.
tests.key: handoffCopy › asks for a wait short enough for a host to return, in both prompts

tests.description: The prompt used to end "do not summarise back to me in chat", and an agent obeying it wrote questions and went silent — leaving the person who pasted the prompt with no idea anything was owed from them. Tool replies are invisible to them; chat is not. Both prompts must send the agent there.
tests.key: handoffCopy › asks the agent to say in chat what it did and what is needed next

tests.description: An agent reading this page needs a command it can RUN. The prose hint names the door; this is the door, and it has to name the origin the page is actually being served from or it points at the wrong machine.
tests.key: handoffCopy › builds an MCP command naming the given origin

tests.description: On the server render the browser's own address is not knowable, so the endpoint degrades to the relative path — still true, still the right address, and it simply assumes the reader knows what host they are on.
tests.key: handoffCopy › degrades the endpoint to a relative path with no origin

tests.description: The reason the `worked` flag exists. "No one is on this yet" is simply false on a map carrying an agent's work, and a person who reads a false sentence about their own map stops trusting the true ones beside it.
tests.key: handoffCopy › does not claim nobody is on a map an agent has already worked

tests.description: The server render has no origin yet. `npm run mcp` is correct only for someone in this checkout, but it is the one of the two that cannot be WRONG — a guessed origin would send an agent somewhere that is not this app.
tests.key: handoffCopy › falls back to npm run mcp when no origin is known

tests.description: The claim the browser tab makes about itself. A tab whose entire point is "this route needs nothing pasted anywhere" would contradict itself the moment it carried something to copy, and an absent field is what a renderer reads to draw no box at all.
tests.key: handoffCopy › gives the browser route nothing to copy

tests.description: Both cases render the same instruction block, so a brief-only map must not arrive with the steps missing.
tests.key: handoffCopy › gives the same instruction and steps for a brief-only map

tests.description: The endpoint an agent that is NOT Claude Code needs. This is the fact the panel previously never stated: a reader holding ChatGPT desktop or Cursor cannot run `claude mcp add`, and the raw address is their half of it.
tests.key: handoffCopy › hands any agent the bare endpoint for the given origin

tests.description: The full band's wording is unchanged for a map nothing has touched — the demoted variant must not leak into the first-meeting case.
tests.key: handoffCopy › keeps the original wording for an untouched map

tests.description: The headline is the panel's first line at heading weight. It has to name the action — a label that only restates the eyebrow would put the panel back to explaining itself before it says what to do.
tests.key: handoffCopy › leads with an instruction naming the agent handoff

tests.description: A brief-only map has no sentence. Interpolating an empty one would leave stray quote marks around nothing, which reads as lost text.
tests.key: handoffCopy › leaves no empty quotes in the prompt when there is no seed idea

tests.description: The panel is only useful if it names a way out, and the tool is what makes the next idea automatic rather than another copy-paste.
tests.key: handoffCopy › names await_new_map as the way to stop copying prompts by hand

tests.description: Without the id the prompt is useless — an agent handed it has no way to know which of the person's maps they meant.
tests.key: handoffCopy › names the map id in the start prompt

tests.description: The load-bearing claim of the whole panel. Nothing is attached, so nothing may be described as in progress or on its way.
tests.key: handoffCopy › never claims work is underway or an agent is coming

tests.description: The three routes, in the order a reader meets them. Pinned as a list because the panel's whole shape depends on there being exactly three alternatives — a fourth appended without thought, or one quietly dropped, changes what the tab strip is claiming about the ways in.
tests.key: handoffCopy › offers exactly the browser, any-agent and Claude Code routes

tests.description: A brief-only map has little or nothing in the seed idea, so read_map would show the agent the emptier of the two things it could read.
tests.key: handoffCopy › points at read_brief when the map was started from a brief

tests.description: An ordinary map started from a sentence: the map is the thing to read.
tests.key: handoffCopy › points at read_map for a map started from a sentence

tests.description: The Claude Code tab is a SHORTCUT for the endpoint beside it, so the two must point at the same place. Spelled as a containment check because one is a bare address and the other wraps it in a command.
tests.key: handoffCopy › points the Claude Code shortcut at the same endpoint as the any-agent tab

tests.description: A returning agent needs a cursor that includes the person's unread work, otherwise it starts again from an earlier state and misses their answers.
tests.key: handoffCopy › puts the known revision in a worked map resume prompt

tests.description: The person's own words carry the context an agent needs, so a sentence-map prompt should hand them over rather than making the agent go and look.
tests.key: handoffCopy › quotes the seed idea in the prompt when there is one

tests.description: Every field renders directly; an empty one would be a blank row in the card.
tests.key: handoffCopy › returns non-empty copy for every field in both cases

tests.description: Saying the idea is saved is the reassurance that replaces the false one — the person's first worry on an empty map is that their input was lost.
tests.key: handoffCopy › says the idea is saved

tests.description: Copying is the first move and pasting the second, so the steps have to be in that order. A set of instructions that reads paste-then-copy is worse than no instructions.
tests.key: handoffCopy › states copying before pasting

tests.description: The prompt is the useful half in BOTH states, so demoting the band must not have quietly dropped the id an agent needs to find the map.
tests.key: handoffCopy › still names the map in the worked variant’s prompt

tests.description: Both entry points start an agent turn, so both must explicitly tell it to wait after writing questions rather than treating the first turn as done.
tests.key: handoffCopy › tells the agent to keep waiting after it writes questions

tests.description: The sentence the panel never said. Someone who has just pressed return needs to be told the prompt goes into an agent's chat window — knowing that is not obvious to anyone who does not already know the answer, and it is the one instruction that turns a quoted block into a next step.
tests.key: handoffCopy › tells the person to paste the prompt into an agent chat window

tests.description: The lookup the colour rule rests on — an answer can only wear its card's colour if the card can be traced to a theme.
tests.key: hueByNodeId › gives a node the hue of its theme

tests.description: Every answer on a themeless map renders neutral — the ordinary early state of a board, not a failure.
tests.key: hueByNodeId › is empty for a map with no themes at all

tests.description: The root idea belongs to no theme. It has no colour to claim, so it must not borrow one.
tests.key: hueByNodeId › leaves out a node that belongs to no theme

tests.description: Neutral, not broken: a default hue would claim a theme the answer does not belong to.
tests.key: hueByNodeId › leaves out a node whose theme is gone

tests.description: A negative index should not be reachable, but a non-negative modulo costs one expression and the alternative is a negative hue that paints nothing.
tests.key: hueForIndex › does not produce a negative hue from a negative index

tests.description: Pure and total: the same index always gives the same colour, which is what lets a theme's hue be recomputed on every render instead of stored, and what makes the same map look identical on two screens.
tests.key: hueForIndex › is deterministic

tests.description: THE promise, and the whole reason the golden angle was chosen over slicing the wheel into N: theme 11 has to be as findable as theme 1 was, without anyone knowing in advance that there would be twelve. A fixed palette cannot make this claim and a model picking "a nice pink" certainly cannot.
tests.key: hueForIndex › keeps the first twelve themes mutually distinguishable

tests.description: The first three are written as literals into every board fixture. Pinning them here is what stops the fixtures and the function drifting apart in silence: a capture would still render, just in colours the palette no longer produces.
tests.key: hueForIndex › starts on the magenta the mockups were drawn around

tests.description: Every CSS colour function reads a hue outside [0,360) as invalid rather than as wrapping, so a theme past the fourth or fifth would simply fail to paint. The wrap has to happen here.
tests.key: hueForIndex › stays a whole number on the wheel however far around it goes

tests.description: Shows that a real cluster was written to the directory it was handed, rather than to the module's own default.
tests.key: initialiseCluster › creates a cluster in the directory it is given

tests.description: The `finally` cleanup: a plaintext password must not survive setup.
tests.key: initialiseCluster › deletes the initdb password file once the cluster is made

tests.description: `dev` runs setup on every start, so this is the guard standing between a container restart and a wiped development database.
tests.key: initialiseCluster › keeps an existing cluster instead of rebuilding it

tests.description: The permission Postgres insists on. Asserted on the bits that matter (group and other), so a stricter umask elsewhere cannot make this flap.
tests.key: initialiseCluster › leaves the data directory unreadable to group and other

tests.description: The server has the JSON string the column stores; the browser usually has the array. Both have to work, or one of the two callers reads no provenance at all while looking like it succeeded.
tests.key: insightStream › accepts the stored JSON string as well as a parsed array

tests.description: The rule the whole module exists to hold in ONE place. A themed node of an insight kind is a card inside its row; only a themeless one is a claim about the whole idea. Getting this wrong draws the same node twice.
tests.key: insightStream › counts a themeless insight and ignores the same kind inside a theme

tests.description: A `problem` or a `goal` is a piece of the idea, not a claim about it. The kind set is a design decision, so moving a kind in or out of it should have to be done deliberately rather than by editing a filter.
tests.key: insightStream › counts only the kinds that are a claim about the whole idea

tests.description: The other half of the same rule: an answer given BEFORE the insight was written is what the insight was drawn from, not something it is behind.
tests.key: insightStream › does not count answers that predate the insight

tests.description: Nothing is hidden by being stale. An insight the thinking has moved past is still worth reading, and dropping it would silently shrink the board.
tests.key: insightStream › keeps a stale insight in the list rather than dropping it

tests.description: A batch written in one transaction shares a timestamp to the millisecond. `getMap` already ordered them, so a tie must leave them alone rather than shuffling them by a tiebreak nobody chose.
tests.key: insightStream › leaves insights written in the same instant in the order they arrived

tests.description: Staleness is "the thinking has moved on since this was written", and it is read off timestamps rather than the event log — which is what lets this module stay pure and serve both the server and the browser.
tests.key: insightStream › marks an insight stale once answers have landed after it

tests.description: The number the standing ask reports. It is measured from the NEWEST insight, because that is what "how far behind are you" means — an old stale insight should not make a board that was just topped up read as behind.
tests.key: insightStream › measures answersSinceNewest from the newest insight only

tests.description: Newest first, which is the order both the ask and the board read.
tests.key: insightStream › orders insights newest first

tests.description: The point of the provenance pointer: the person can see the thinking behind a claim instead of taking it on trust.
tests.key: insightStream › resolves the questions an insight came out of

tests.description: Day one, and the state every capture actually produces. All zeros rather than a thrown error or a partly-filled object, because the surface that renders this has to read a brand-new map without a special case.
tests.key: insightStream › returns all zeros for a map with nothing on it

tests.description: A node arriving over JSON carries `undefined` where the database row carried null. An insight that silently stopped counting for that reason would be the precise drift this module exists to prevent.
tests.key: insightStream › treats an absent themeId the same as a null one

tests.description: Read on every `read_map`. One bad row written by an older agent must not be able to take down the map's entire rendering.
tests.key: insightStream › yields no citations for a malformed or absent value rather than throwing

tests.description: What makes a card show your words as its content, with the question demoted to a label above them. Only a question can reach this state — it is the presence of an answer that earns it, not the status string alone.
tests.key: isAnsweredCard › is an answered question and nothing else

tests.description: An insight carries `status: 'answered'` all over the seed data — it is how a settled claim is marked. It is still not something YOU answered, and drawing it with a pencil would invite editing the partner's own thinking as though it were your reply.
tests.key: isAnsweredCard › never treats a settled insight as your answer

tests.description: A mapped PUBLIC address is still public — the unwrapping must not turn into a blanket refusal of the mapped form.
tests.key: isBlockedAddress › allows a mapped public address

tests.description: Ordinary public IPv6 has to work.
tests.key: isBlockedAddress › allows a public IPv6 address

tests.description: The whole point is that ordinary public addresses go through.
tests.key: isBlockedAddress › allows ordinary public addresses

tests.description: The bypass that makes an IPv6-unaware check useless: every blocked v4 range can be written as a v6 address, and has to be judged as the v4 address it actually is.
tests.key: isBlockedAddress › blocks IPv4 addresses wearing an IPv6 mapping

tests.description: IPv6 loopback and unspecified, in both the compressed forms they arrive in.
tests.key: isBlockedAddress › blocks IPv6 loopback and unspecified

tests.description: Unique-local and link-local are v6's private ranges.
tests.key: isBlockedAddress › blocks IPv6 unique-local and link-local

tests.description: A zone id is a local routing detail, and anything carrying one is link-local anyway — parsing must not choke on the suffix and let it past.
tests.key: isBlockedAddress › blocks a link-local address carrying a zone id

tests.description: Loopback reaches every other service bound on the same box — an admin panel, a database, the app's own unauthenticated internals.
tests.key: isBlockedAddress › blocks loopback across the whole /8, not just 127.0.0.1

tests.description: The single most valuable address to an attacker: on every major cloud it serves the instance's own credentials to anything that asks.
tests.key: isBlockedAddress › blocks the cloud metadata endpoint

tests.description: Carrier-grade NAT, benchmarking, multicast, the reserved top sixteenth, and the unspecified address — none of them is a page.
tests.key: isBlockedAddress › blocks the other non-public v4 ranges

tests.description: The three private blocks are the rest of whatever network this server sits inside.
tests.key: isBlockedAddress › blocks the private ranges

tests.description: The edges of 172.16/12 specifically, because it is the one range whose boundaries are easy to get wrong by an octet.
tests.key: isBlockedAddress › gets the edges of the 172.16/12 block right

tests.description: Anything that is not a resolved address at all is a surprise, and a surprise here has to fail closed rather than open.

tests.description: Not everything with a slash in it is an address.

tests.description: Whitespace around a pasted address is normal and is not the person's mistake to fix.

tests.description: A drag could settle several nodes at once, so a batch is the shape of the request.

tests.description: Without a node id there is nothing to move.

tests.description: A null or non-object entry must be reported, not thrown on.

tests.description: An empty batch asks for nothing and is more likely a bug than an intent.

tests.description: A blank or non-string entry would render as an unlabelled button nobody could interpret, so it is dropped rather than shown.

tests.description: An empty array is the same situation as no column at all.

tests.description: Valid JSON of the wrong shape is still not a list of suggestions.

tests.description: A malformed column must not take the card down with it.
tests.key: parseOptions › offers no chips when the column is not valid JSON

tests.description: A question with no shortlist is the ordinary case, not a degraded one — the card is simply a card with an answer box.
tests.key: parseOptions › offers no chips when the column is null

tests.description: The stored shape: a JSON array of strings, because SQLite has no arrays.

tests.description: Every reader is fed untrusted JSON from the log, where a row may predate the current shape or have failed to parse at all.

tests.description: An errored call has nothing to ask about — putting a prompt on screen off the back of a failure would be worse than showing nothing.

tests.description: A tool that is not ask_user, or a result with no questions, must leave the caller returning the server's response untouched.
tests.key: pendingQuestions › asks nothing when the result carries no questions

tests.description: A malformed entry is dropped rather than rendered as an undefined prompt.
tests.key: pendingQuestions › drops entries that are not a well-formed question

tests.description: The normal hand-off: the server wrote the questions and the page now has somebody to ask.
tests.key: pendingQuestions › reads the questions out of a pending ask_user result

tests.description: Completion is read off the NEWEST round only, so a question abandoned three rounds ago cannot hold the loop hostage — it stays answerable and stops gating. The caller passes the newest round's count; this pins that the module honours it rather than looking any wider.
tests.key: pendingRow › advances on the newest round alone, whatever older rounds left open

tests.description: Each status gets its OWN sentence — a shared one would make the distinction above invisible on screen even though the logic drew it.
tests.key: pendingRow › gives each presence state a distinct sentence

tests.description: `next-steps` is where the loop ARRIVES. Reaching for a further round there would promise a continuation the product does not have.
tests.key: pendingRow › hides at the end of the loop

tests.description: Nothing has been drawn, so there is no round to reach past.
tests.key: pendingRow › hides when the map has no rounds at all

tests.description: The cards are the action while questions are open. A placeholder below them would be the page reaching for something the person has not finished giving.
tests.key: pendingRow › hides while the newest round still has open questions

tests.description: The pending row also appears on a DAY-ONE map — a seed idea nobody has picked up, with no answers on it at all — so no sentence may name answers the person has not given. This is the assertion that keeps the wording true in both cases rather than only in the end-of-round one.
tests.key: pendingRow › never claims answers exist, since a day-one map has none

tests.description: The three sentences are the honest part, and they are genuinely different claims — "has everything you have added" is only true of an agent whose turn is running.
tests.key: pendingRow › says an agent has what you added only when one is actually in a turn

tests.description: Attached but idle: it will see the answers when its turn comes round, which is a weaker claim and has to read as one.
tests.key: pendingRow › says an attached agent is waiting for its turn, not working

tests.description: The state every preview and capture actually produces, and the one most at risk of being quietly dressed up as one of the other two. It must never claim an agent is there.
tests.key: pendingRow › says plainly that nothing can reach the page when nothing can

tests.description: The round is done and the poll may still bring a new one: this is the whole point of the feature — the page moves before anybody asks it to.
tests.key: pendingRow › shimmers as soon as the round is answered

tests.description: Bounded, not indefinite. A row that shimmered forever would be claiming an agent was writing, which is the one thing this page can never know.
tests.key: pendingRow › stops shimmering once the wait runs out

tests.description: Non-strings are dropped rather than coerced: a numeric option is a mistake, and rendering it as "1" would hide the mistake behind a plausible chip.
tests.key: planMapMutations suggested answers › drops non-string options rather than stringifying them

tests.description: The field is additive: every node the model already knew how to send still plans exactly as it did, carrying no options.
tests.key: planMapMutations suggested answers › leaves a node that predates the field unchanged

tests.description: The ordinary path: a shortlist survives as the JSON array the column holds.
tests.key: planMapMutations suggested answers › serialises a question’s suggested answers to a JSON array

tests.description: An empty array must not become a stored empty array — that would render a chip row holding nothing.
tests.key: planMapMutations suggested answers › stores nothing for an empty option list

tests.description: A list of blanks is the same situation as an empty list.
tests.key: planMapMutations suggested answers › stores nothing when every option is blank

tests.description: Anything that is not a list at all is not a shortlist.
tests.key: planMapMutations suggested answers › stores nothing when options is not an array

tests.description: Most questions have no obvious shortlist, and that is not a degraded case.
tests.key: planMapMutations suggested answers › stores nothing when the model offered no options

tests.description: Blank steps are dropped before the length is judged, so three steps of which two are whitespace is still not a flow.

tests.description: The ordinary case: steps survive in order, and the note with them.
tests.key: planMapMutations — a node carrying a diagram › keeps a well-formed shape, steps in order

tests.description: A node that never mentioned a diagram is the ordinary case and must come through carrying none.
tests.key: planMapMutations — a node carrying a diagram › leaves a node with no diagram alone

tests.description: The note is optional, and its absence must not leave the key present with an empty value — the card renders a caption line for anything truthy.
tests.key: planMapMutations — a node carrying a diagram › omits the note entirely rather than carrying an empty one

tests.description: One step is not a flow — it is a sentence, and it would draw as a single box with an arrow pointing at nothing.
tests.key: planMapMutations — a node carrying a diagram › rejects a shape too short to be a flow

tests.description: Anything that is not a shape at all produces no diagram rather than a throw that would take the whole turn down with it.
tests.key: planMapMutations — a node carrying a diagram › survives junk where a shape was expected

tests.description: NO HUE IS ASSIGNED HERE, and the absence is the point. The hue depends on how many themes the map already has, which this pure function cannot see — and the split (the agent names the theme, the app colours it) is the whole reason the palette stays mutually distinguishable however many themes an agent invents. This case exists to stop someone "helpfully" adding one.
tests.key: planMapMutations — create_themes › assigns no colour, leaving that to the app

tests.description: A theme with no ref is unreachable — no node could ever name it — so it would be a galaxy on the board with nothing able to orbit it.
tests.key: planMapMutations — create_themes › drops a theme that no node could name

tests.description: A theme with no label draws a hub captioned nothing, and a cluster you cannot identify is worse than a cluster that is not there.
tests.key: planMapMutations — create_themes › drops a theme that would render as an unlabelled cluster

tests.description: A node may name a theme created in the SAME turn, which is how a round normally arrives: open the galaxies, then hang the questions off them.
tests.key: planMapMutations — create_themes › keeps a node’s reference to a theme from the same turn

tests.description: The order they were opened in is also the order they are drawn down the board, so it has to survive planning.
tests.key: planMapMutations — create_themes › keeps the themes in the order they were sent

tests.description: A node naming no theme is the root idea, which belongs to no galaxy precisely because it is what every galaxy orbits.
tests.key: planMapMutations — create_themes › leaves a node that names no theme unattached

tests.description: The ordinary path: a valid theme survives with both the ref a node will name it by and the label its cluster is drawn with.
tests.key: planMapMutations — create_themes › plans a theme with its ref and label intact

tests.description: Malformed input has to survive the way it does for nodes: a non-array, a null entry or a junk scalar produces no themes rather than a throw that would take the whole turn down with it.
tests.key: planMapMutations — create_themes › survives malformed theme input rather than throwing

tests.description: An unknown kind is DROPPED here rather than stored, so a kind added to the vocabulary but not reaching this guard would vanish silently — the agent told the write succeeded, and nothing on the board to show for it.
tests.key: planMapMutations — the forward-looking kinds › accepts a suggestion and an experiment as real nodes

tests.description: Carried verbatim, refs and all. Resolving them here is impossible: a ref usually names a node created moments earlier in this same call, whose real id does not exist until the write.
tests.key: planMapMutations — the sources an insight cites › carries the refs through untouched for applyToolCalls to resolve

tests.description: Non-strings are filtered rather than stringified. `[1, 2]` is a mistake, and turning it into `"1"` would store a citation pointing at nothing while looking like it had worked.
tests.key: planMapMutations — the sources an insight cites › drops non-strings and blanks rather than coercing them

tests.description: The ordinary case, and every node written before this field existed.
tests.key: planMapMutations — the sources an insight cites › leaves a node that cited nothing carrying null

tests.description: The `serialiseOptions` convention: a node that named nothing must be indistinguishable from one that never had the field, rather than carrying an empty array nobody can render.
tests.key: planMapMutations — the sources an insight cites › normalises an empty or all-blank list to null

tests.description: A slice carries the node it would settle. Like parentRef this stays a REF here — resolving it to a real id is applyToolCalls' job — so the plan must hand it through untouched rather than validating it against a map it cannot see.
tests.key: planMapMutations › carries a slice tests ref through as testsRef

tests.description: A kind the map has no treatment for would render as an untyped blob, so it is dropped rather than stored.
tests.key: planMapMutations › drops a node whose kind the map cannot draw

tests.description: An empty pill is worse than no pill — it takes up map space saying nothing.
tests.key: planMapMutations › drops a node with a blank label

tests.description: An unrecognised status would fall through to the default treatment silently; normalising it makes the fallback explicit.
tests.key: planMapMutations › falls back to answered for an unknown status

tests.description: One turn routinely adds nodes, resolves a question, and moves the phase on.
tests.key: planMapMutations › handles adds, updates and a phase change in one turn

tests.description: An invalid phase must leave the map where it was rather than break the nav.
tests.key: planMapMutations › ignores a phase that is not part of the loop

tests.description: An update naming no real change would be a pointless write.
tests.key: planMapMutations › ignores an update that carries no valid fields

tests.description: Without an id there is nothing to target.
tests.key: planMapMutations › ignores an update with no id

tests.description: "updated" is how the map marks what just changed; it must survive intact.

tests.description: A root idea has no parent, and must not invent one.
tests.key: planMapMutations › leaves parentRef null when none is given

tests.description: An increment that settles nothing is a real state the summary screen reports, so the absent link must survive as null rather than being invented or dropped.
tests.key: planMapMutations › leaves testsRef null when a slice names nothing

tests.description: Sibling position on screen comes from this index.
tests.key: planMapMutations › numbers siblings in the order they arrive

tests.description: The ordinary path: a valid node survives with its fields intact.
tests.key: planMapMutations › plans an insert for a valid node

tests.description: A slice's purpose usually sharpens once the whole sequence is laid out, so the link is editable after the fact.
tests.key: planMapMutations › plans an update to what a slice settles

tests.description: Resolving an answered question is the most common update.
tests.key: planMapMutations › plans an update with only the fields supplied

tests.key: railEntries › renders a full exchange as one line per act

tests.description: A row with no usable name could not be identified or removed, so it is dropped rather than rendered blank.

tests.key: readAttachments › keeps a row that has no file behind it

tests.description: A warning is the whole reason a scanned PDF does not silently become an empty brief, so it has to survive the trip.
tests.key: readBriefResponse › carries a warning through

tests.key: readBriefResponse › falls back to a readable sentence when the body is not JSON

tests.description: A 500 with nothing in it at all — no body to read a reason out of.
tests.key: readBriefResponse › handles an empty body

tests.description: When a route failed the way it meant to, its own sentence is better than anything this function could compose — it knows what actually went wrong.
tests.key: readBriefResponse › prefers the route’s own error sentence

tests.description: A 200 whose body is missing the one field that makes a brief a brief. The status said fine; the payload is not usable, and saying otherwise would attach an empty brief that looks like a successful read.
tests.key: readBriefResponse › rejects a success response with no text in it

tests.description: The ordinary success, and the shape every caller downstream depends on.
tests.key: readBriefResponse › returns the brief a route handed back

tests.description: A route that saw nothing worth flagging simply omits the key. The readout wants the absence spelled out, so an omitted warning becomes null rather than travelling as undefined and reading as "not decided yet".
tests.key: readBriefResponse › spells an omitted warning as null

tests.description: A failure no route ever saw, so no route could have made it JSON.
tests.key: readJson › describes an HTML error page from a proxy

tests.description: THE REPORTED CASE. An unhandled throw used to reach the browser as a 500 with nothing in it, and reading that as JSON is what put `Unexpected end of JSON input` on screen.
tests.key: readJson › describes an empty error body without a parse error

tests.description: A failing response that IS JSON but carries no `error` field — well-formed and still says nothing, so the fallback has to cover it.
tests.key: readJson › falls back when a failing body states no error

tests.description: A route that named the fix as well as the fault: the sentence is the headline, and everything else it said comes back beside it rather than being dropped on the floor of the network tab.
tests.key: readJson › hands back the rest of a failing body alongside the message

tests.description: Nothing parsed means nothing to offer, and inventing a shape here would put an undefined command in front of a caller that trusts the field.
tests.key: readJson › offers no failure body when there was nothing to parse

tests.description: A route that failed the way it meant to. Its own sentence is better than anything composed here, so it wins over the fallback.
tests.key: readJson › prefers the error a failing route stated itself

tests.description: Production withholds the fix, so there is nothing to hand back — and the absence has to read as absence rather than as an empty pill.
tests.key: readJson › reports no extra fields when the route withheld them

tests.description: The ordinary case: a route answered, and the caller gets the payload.
tests.key: readJson › returns the parsed body of a successful response

tests.description: A 200 is not on its own a reason to trust the body: a truncated one still has to fail as a sentence rather than as a thrown SyntaxError.
tests.key: readJson › treats a truncated body as a failure even on a 200

tests.description: The fallback is used verbatim, so each call site's wording reaches the person who was doing that particular thing.
tests.key: readJson › uses the caller wording rather than a generic one

tests.description: The payload round-trips through a text column, so a reader must get the object back rather than the string.
tests.key: readSince › decodes stored payloads back into objects

tests.description: A caught-up agent must still leave holding a usable cursor, or it has no way to ask again.
tests.key: readSince › reports the current revision even when the delta is empty

tests.description: A cursor means "only what I have not seen", which is what stops an agent re-ingesting its own writes as new information.
tests.key: readSince › returns only what happened after the cursor

tests.description: No cursor means "give me everything", which is what a fresh agent needs.
tests.key: readSince › returns the whole log when given no cursor

tests.description: The same degrade-to-null contract the other JSON columns keep: a card that cannot render its tradeoffs is still a thing worth trying, and one that took the board down with it would not be.

tests.description: Each requirement gets its own bullet, so a blank one is a bullet with nothing after it — a thing you either have or do not, unnamed.
tests.key: readTradeoffs › drops blank requirements rather than printing empty bullets

tests.description: Every field is optional. An agent that knows the effort but not the cost should say the effort rather than inventing a cost to fill the shape.
tests.key: readTradeoffs › keeps a partial answer rather than demanding the whole shape

tests.description: An object with nothing usable in it is nothing, not an empty panel. A card that drew a "Tradeoffs" heading over no bullets would be announcing thinking that had not happened.
tests.key: readTradeoffs › reads an object with nothing in it as nothing

tests.description: The whole shape, round-tripped. Every field is optional, so this is the only place the full set is asserted together.
tests.key: readTradeoffs › reads what a way forward would cost and what it would cost you

tests.description: These print in a fixed label column, where leading space is visible as a value that does not line up with the one above it.
tests.key: readTradeoffs › trims what it keeps

tests.description: Day one. A map that has done nothing wrong should read an invitation, not a shortfall — and the empty case is the one every fresh map produces.

tests.description: The full read. Without this the agent is told the map's contents and left to invent its own sense of whether it owes anything.
tests.key: read_map carries the standing ask › reports the budget on a full read

tests.description: The delta branch is the one a WORKING agent actually calls. An ask that appeared only on the full read would be an ask the agent saw once, on its first turn, and never again — which is the difference between a mechanism that works and one that reads well in a diff.
tests.key: read_map carries the standing ask › reports the same budget on a delta read

tests.description: The bump and the insert share a transaction, so the map's own revision must agree with the last event written.
tests.key: recordEvents › leaves the map at the revision of its last event

tests.description: The revision must advance once per event and the returned events must carry the revisions they were given, or an agent's cursor points at nothing.
tests.key: recordEvents › mints one revision per event and returns them in order

tests.description: An empty batch is not an error — it is a caller whose plan produced no changes, and it must not move the revision.
tests.key: recordEvents › records nothing and holds the revision for an empty batch

tests.description: Writing to a map that does not exist must fail loudly rather than minting a revision nobody can read.
tests.key: recordEvents › refuses to write against an unknown map

tests.description: A retry must see everything the first attempt wrote, not just its first row.
tests.key: recordEvents › returns every event the original call wrote on a retry

tests.description: The idempotency key is what makes an agent's retry safe. Without it a timed-out call that is retried inserts the same nodes twice.
tests.key: recordEvents › treats a repeated requestId as a no-op and returns the original revision

tests.description: Order is the point of an ordered log.
tests.key: renderEvents › keeps events in the order given, one per line

tests.description: The revision leads because it is what the agent passes back as its cursor.
tests.key: renderEvents › leads every line with the revision, kind and origin

tests.description: An empty string is not a gist — appending a bare dash would be noise.
tests.key: renderEvents › omits the dash when the readable field is empty

tests.description: `label` wins over the others so a node event reads as the node, not as whatever incidental text happens to ride along with it.
tests.key: renderEvents › prefers the label when an event carries several readable fields

tests.description: An agent that asked for a delta and got nothing must be told so plainly — an empty string reads as a broken tool.

tests.description: Each kind carries its readable part under a different key. A wall of bare kinds would tell the agent nothing about what actually changed.
tests.key: renderEvents › shows the gist from whichever field the kind uses

tests.description: A payload that failed to decode arrives as null. One bad row must not take down the agent's whole catch-up read.
tests.key: renderEvents › still renders an event whose payload is null or empty

tests.description: The supported host: the work is handed to the browser so it can surface the tab first, and the result still comes back to the caller.

tests.description: A rejection is the agent's to handle. Swallowing it here would settle a pending question with nothing and leave the agent waiting on a turn that already failed.

tests.key: requestUserInteraction › runs the work directly when the host does not support it

tests.description: No agent at all — an ordinary browser, or a captured scenario — takes the same path rather than throwing on a missing model context.
tests.key: requestUserInteraction › runs the work directly when there is no model context

tests.description: The message is the only instruction a developer gets at the moment the app refuses to boot, so it has to name the file that explains what to do.

tests.description: The happy path still has to work: a configured string is passed through unchanged, with no normalising or rewriting that could corrupt a DSN.

tests.description: A ref that is not in the plan is usually the real id of something already on the board, so it passes through untouched.
tests.key: resolveRef › passes through a value the plan does not name

tests.description: The ordinary case: a node names something created moments earlier in the same call, and the ref has to become the id the database just handed back.

tests.description: The name reaches a DROP SCHEMA statement. A label carrying a quote should produce a dull name rather than a broken — or dangerous — statement.
tests.key: uniqueSchemaName › reduces anything outside [a-z0-9_] to an underscore

tests.description: It asks for something rather than only reporting an absence — the point is to get the section dealt with on the agent's next turn.
tests.key: untouchedNoteText › asks the agent to act rather than only reporting the gap

tests.description: It names the section both ways: the mark the person just clicked, and the heading, so the agent can find it without another round trip.
tests.key: untouchedNoteText › names the section by mark and heading

tests.description: Without the separator the new key would be glued onto the end of the last line, producing a key nothing can read back.
tests.key: upsertEnvLine › adds a newline before the key when the file lacks a trailing one

tests.description: The first run on a fresh clone has no `.env.local` at all, so writing the key into empty text is the ordinary path rather than an edge case.

tests.description: A developer who wrote `export DATABASE_URL=` still declared the key, so it is replaced rather than duplicated alongside the export form.

tests.description: The busy flag has to clear on both paths, or the button stays dead after one failure.

tests.description: In an isolated scenario there is no map to advance. It must be inert, not throw — the same way the map is readable without a bridge.

tests.description: `next-steps` has nowhere further to go, and neither does an unknown phase.

tests.description: It calls the same tool through the same route an agent would, rather than reaching around it — so there is one implementation of what a phase set is.

tests.description: The note names the phase in the words the nav uses, so someone reading the log and someone reading the screen see the same vocabulary.
tests.key: useAdvancePhase › names the destination phase in the note

tests.description: The phase is server-rendered, so without this the nav would keep showing the old step until something else happened to refresh the page.
tests.key: useAdvancePhase › re-reads the page once the phase has moved

tests.description: A declined write must not leave the button claiming success.
tests.key: useAdvancePhase › reports a failed phase write

tests.description: And it must not say the note was lost, because it was not — it is on the log, and telling someone otherwise is its own small dishonesty.

tests.description: Without a bridge the phase still moves. The note is the part that needs somewhere to go, not the phase set.

tests.description: A network throw is the same story as a declined write, not a crash.
